The FOMC statement is macro-positive (strong labor market, solid household spending, inflation near 2 percent), but the contemporaneous SLOOS points to a more restrictive credit channel than the statement alone suggests. Banks reported tighter lending standards for C&I loans and for construction and land development loans, broadly tighter other terms across firm sizes, and weaker demand for construction and land development credit. These SLOOS signals imply headwinds for business fixed investment and CRE activity—aligning with the FOMC’s note that capex had already moderated—and they reinforce the Financial Stability Report’s caution around elevated valuations and high corporate leverage. Netting these, the outlook remains positive but more cautiously so, with downside risks incrementally higher than implied by the statement alone.
